MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron has no single lexical trigger — it fires mildly on ordinary tokens inside fluent, well-edited prose (news/marketing narrative) and is strongly *suppressed* throughout repetitive, keyword-stuffed SEO/product-spam text, so it effectively acts as a "natural prose vs. keyword-spam" register detector.

This neuron is only weakly selective: it fires on mid-clause function words/word-fragments in narrative prose, especially in constructions describing unrealized or long-presumed states ("she never got to be", "was always thought to have been", "are originally from", "the long and rolling highway") — the same tokens (e.g. "never", "have") appear with strong negative activation in other contexts, so it reflects context-dependent modulation rather than a fixed lexical trigger.
